readout_other: CRS-R total score and CRS-R index; BOLD fMRI during sonication; psychophysiological interaction connectivity; resting-state connectivity
direction_notes: Behavioural responsiveness (CRS-R) increased linearly over the two sessions; BOLD signal was reduced in one ipsilateral temporal cluster during sonication, and connectivity of the targeted thalamus increased with three cortical clusters.
safety_notes: One adverse event (a respiratory infection) was judged unrelated to LIFU; no change in vital parameters during sonication.

target.label: central thalamus (caudal CL nucleus and CM-PF complex), preferentially left

timing.protocol_description: Ten 30-second on blocks separated by 30 s off periods, delivered inside the MRI. Two sessions one week apart (one patient received one), each with CRS-R assessments before and after.

source_quotes.n_subjects: This convenience sample included 10 chronic DOC patients (see Table 1; DOC at entry, 6 male, mean: age = 39.1, time since injury [TSI] = 56.75 months, 4/6 anoxic/traumatic injury) referred to the study by longterm care facilities and private households following the persistence of DOC past the 1-year post-injury period.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: A second, identical, cycle of LIFU and assesssments were performed in all but one subject (C5; excluded due to infection).
